statement.p: Consider the graphs of f(x) and g(x) below:

image.shortdescription: Graph of two functions and some points on the functions.

description.p: Function f starts at the origin, goes up and back down to the x-axis and then up higher and then back down to the axis again, with the two peaks at x=2.2 and x=6.1. It hits the x-axis at x=0, x=4, and x=8. Function g is an increasing line going though the points occuring at the two peaks of f, that is, (2.2, f(2.2)) and (6.1,f(6.1)).

statement.p: For each interval given below, decide whether the average rate of change of f(x) or g(x) is greater over that particular interval.

row.cell: Which function has GREATER average rate of change?

ul.name: AnSwEr0001
ul.li: both have an equal rate of change

ul.name: AnSwEr0002
ul.li: both have an equal rate of change

ul.name: AnSwEr0003
ul.li: both have an equal rate of change

ul.name: AnSwEr0004
ul.li: both have an equal rate of change

ul.name: AnSwEr0005
ul.li: both have an equal rate of change

p.m: \text{both have an equal rate of change}

solution.p: Since the graph of g(x) is a line, its average rate of change is the same over all intervals. Since the graph of g(x) is going up, its average rate of change is always positive. The average rate of change of f(x) is clearly changing depending on the interval. If the slope of the line connecting the two endpoints of the interval on f(x) is going up and is steeper than the slope of g(x), then the average rate of change of f(x) will be greater over that interval. If the line connecting the two endpoints points on f(x) is less steep, horizontal, or going down, then the average rate of change of g(x) will greater over that interval. If the slope of the line connecting to endpoints of the interval on f(x) is the same as the slope of g(x), then the two average rates of change will be equal (such as the case for the interval 2.2 \leq x \leq 6.1. Based on this consideration, you should determine the following answers:

row.cell: Which function has GREATER average rate of change?
both have an equal rate of change
